name: Antala Industries
summary: Antala Industries makes BOPP bags, BOPP printing and lamination rolls and PP woven bags for food processing, fertiliser, chemical, cement and seed customers from a single plant in Rajkot, Gujarat; it began as the partnership firm Octagon Industries in 2021 and became a company in August 2024. Total income grew from ₹12.6 cr in FY24 to ₹47.5 cr in FY26 and profit rose 133% in FY26 to ₹4.24 cr, with debt to equity low at 0.25. The whole ₹23.33 cr issue is fresh, with ₹10.68 cr for working capital and ₹5.89 cr for new machinery, and promoters keep about 52% after the issue. At the upper band the post-issue P/E on FY26 profit is about 19.2x, below the median of the two listed peers named in the offer document, while the top 10 customers still make up 56% of revenue.

checks.name: Revenue growth
checks.finding: Total income rose from ₹12.59 cr (FY24) to ₹47.53 cr (FY26), a CAGR of about 94%.

checks.name: Revenue rose every year
checks.finding: Total income grew every year: ₹12.59 cr, ₹31.98 cr, ₹47.53 cr (FY24–FY26).

checks.name: Debt to equity
checks.finding: Debt to equity was 0.25 in FY26 (borrowings ₹4.19 cr vs net worth ₹17.03 cr), and 0.08 at September 2026.

checks.name: Debt growing slower than revenue
checks.finding: Borrowings rose from ₹0.36 cr to ₹4.19 cr over FY24–FY26, far faster than the 3.8x rise in total income, though they fell to ₹1.75 cr by September 2026.

checks.name: Net worth rising
checks.finding: Net worth rose every year: ₹3.54 cr, ₹12.19 cr, ₹17.03 cr (FY24–FY26), and ₹22.17 cr at September 2026.

checks.name: Positive operating cash flow
checks.finding: Operating cash flow figures were not found in public sources.

checks.name: Profit growth
checks.finding: Profit after tax grew about 133% in FY26, to ₹4.24 cr from ₹1.82 cr.

checks.name: Profit margin trend
checks.finding: Net margin moved from 7.1% (FY24) to 5.7% (FY25) and 8.9% (FY26), higher than three years ago.

checks.name: Return on equity
